headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES: 7.38 g/t AuEq OVER 35.7 METRES INCLUDING VISIBLE GOLD AT SUREBET — GOLDEN TRIANGLE DISCOVERY STILL OPEN
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSX-V: GOT) released August 21 drill results from its high-grade Surebet discovery in BC's Golden Triangle, with hole GD-26-436 returning 7.38 g/t AuEq over 35.7 metres including a 19.51 g/t AuEq subinterval over 8.32 metres — multiple occurrences of visible gold were noted throughout. The company has now completed 52 of 98 planned 2026 holes (31,994 metres total), all intersecting quartz-sulphide mineralization, while metallurgical testwork confirms 92.2% gold and 86.5% silver recoveries using gravity and flotation. For retail investors tracking early-stage discovery leverage in British Columbia, the combination of near-surface high grades, open geometry in multiple directions, and confirmed metallurgical performance is the hallmark of a discovery that could support a significant resource estimate.

headline: WESTHAVEN DRILLS 12 g/t GOLD AND 103 g/t SILVER BELOW PROPOSED SHOVELNOSE STOPES — PREFEASIBILITY STUDY FED NEW RESOURCE DATA
snippet: Westhaven Gold (TSX-V: WHN) reported August 20 that hole SNR26-117 returned 10.04 metres grading 12.18 g/t gold and 103 g/t silver from the Shovelnose South Zone — extending mineralization below the deepest stopes proposed in the company's 2025 preliminary economic assessment. A second hole, SNR26-110, intersected 37.34 metres grading 6.24 g/t gold and 55 g/t silver at the southeastern deposit margin. The 35,000-metre resource infill program is more than 76% complete with four active drills, feeding into an updated mineral resource estimate to support a prefeasibility study targeting completion in the second half of 2027. For investors tracking TSX-V development-stage gold-silver plays, discovering grade below the current mine plan boundary directly expands project NPV at today's $4,600+ gold and $70+ silver prices.

headline: APEX CONFIRMS MONAZITE AND BASTNAESITE HOST REE AT RIFT — NEBRASKA PROJECT USES THE SAME MINERALS AS 85% OF GLOBAL RARE EARTH PRODUCTION
snippet: Apex Critical Metals (CSE: APXC) reported August 20 that quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis of four drillholes at its Rift Rare Earth Project in southeastern Nebraska confirms REE mineralization is hosted predominantly within monazite and bastnaesite — the two minerals responsible for the substantial majority of global rare earth oxide production and well-established in commercial processing circuits. This follows August 12 drill results including 4.48% REO over 8.0 metres and 5.27% REO over 10.2 metres within broader 150-metre-plus intervals exceeding 2.00% REO in the Trinity Zone. The company is targeting a mineral resource estimate in the first half of 2027 from a 22,000-25,000-metre drill campaign. Confirmed processability in dominant commercial minerals is a critical de-risking milestone that separates Rift from exotic-mineralogy rare earth projects that face additional metallurgical development.

headline: GDXJ BREAKS OUT OF 4-MONTH FALLING WEDGE — JUNIOR GOLD MINERS FINALLY CATCH BULLION'S BULL RUN AFTER 41% SELLOFF
snippet: The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) surged 7.4% in a single session, breaking the upper resistance of a falling-wedge pattern that had built for 4.7 months — ending a brutal 41.3% selloff that had disconnected junior miners from gold's bull run. GDXJ was trading at $132.45 on August 21, while GDX has gained 23.75% in August with retail inflows reaching $419 million — on pace for the ETF's strongest monthly intake since February. The top 25 GDXJ components averaged all-in sustaining costs of approximately $1,436 per ounce against an average realized gold price near $4,873, implying a $3,437 per ounce unit profit — margins that rival the best quarters in the sector's history. For retail investors who watched gold run from $3,000 to $4,600 while GDXJ lost ground, the technical and fundamental breakout signals the junior mining equity risk premium may finally be compressing.

headline: GOLD MINERS GENERATE RECORD $2,800/oz MARGINS AS AISC FALLS 5% WHILE GOLD PRICES SURGE 24% — WIDEST SPREAD IN HISTORY
snippet: Global average all-in sustaining costs for gold producers are on track to decline 5% in 2026 while gold prices have increased approximately 24%, creating record high operating margins of roughly $2,800 per ounce — the widest spread in gold mining history according to S&P Global and industry analysts. A mid-tier producer with AISC of $1,600 per ounce sees its per-ounce margin expand from roughly $400 at $2,000 gold to over $3,000 at current prices — a more than sevenfold expansion. Combined with the GDX's August retail inflow surge and the GDXJ's technical breakout from a prolonged selloff, the fundamental and sentiment case for gold mining equities is converging for the first time in this bull cycle. For TSX-V and ASX investors, the implication is straightforward: senior and mid-tier producer cash flow is now being deployed into exploration and acquisition budgets, which historically drives discovery premiums for junior companies.

headline: JACKSON HOLE WATCH: NEW FED CHAIR WARSH DELIVERS FIRST MAJOR SPEECH AUG 28 — GOLD AT $4,600 AWAITS POLICY SIGNAL
snippet: The Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole Economic Symposium runs August 27-29, with new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivering his first keynote speech as chair on Friday morning August 28 — an event that carries outsized weight because Warsh, who took office May 22, no longer telegraphs the Fed's intentions ahead of meetings, meaning this speech represents genuine information about monetary policy direction. The symposium theme is 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.' Gold, at $4,603 heading into the week, has already priced in rate-cut expectations and a weaker dollar from Treasury buyback expansion; a dovish Warsh would extend the August rally toward $4,650 resistance and beyond, while a hawkish signal could trigger a temporary pullback that analysts have called a buying opportunity. For investors in TSX-V and ASX gold juniors, Jackson Hole is the most important single event of the week — potentially more market-moving than the ADP, GDP, and PCE data releases also scheduled for August 25-26.

headline: FARADAY COPPER CLOSES BHP'S SAN MANUEL IN ARIZONA — COMBINED DISTRICT HOLDS 18 BILLION POUNDS OF COPPER WITH $100M FINANCING
snippet: Faraday Copper (TSX-V: FDY) closed its acquisition of BHP's San Manuel property in Arizona this month, combining it with Faraday's adjacent Copper Creek project to create a multi-generational copper district expected to host more than 18 billion pounds of copper — positioning the company as a major US-jurisdiction copper developer at a time when Washington is aggressively seeking domestic copper supply. BHP received shares equivalent to a 30% fully diluted interest in Faraday, and the company simultaneously announced $100 million in associated financing. San Manuel brings with it a copper mine, land, water rights, and existing infrastructure adjacent to Copper Creek. The transaction is among the largest copper-focused acquisitions by a TSX-V junior this year, and with copper near $13,885 per tonne and the US copper tariff decision still pending, the strategic timing of a domestic copper district play is notable for investors tracking critical minerals M&A.

headline: COPPER RETREATS BELOW $14,000 AS LME STOCKS SURGE 50% IN THREE DAYS — PRE-TARIFF SQUEEZE EASES, BACKWARDATION NARROWS
snippet: LME on-warrant copper inventories rose 63,000 tonnes between Monday and Wednesday this week — the largest three-day increase in months — extending gains for a sixth consecutive session to 123,100 tonnes and reversing the prolonged supply squeeze that had pushed copper near $14,000 per tonne. The LME cash/3-month copper spread narrowed sharply to approximately $248 per tonne after recently hitting levels last seen during the 2021 copper exchange squeeze, as fresh metal deliveries from Asian and European warehouses eased the tightness. Three-month LME copper fell below $14,000 per tonne, posting its sharpest decline since July 23. For junior copper explorer investors, the inventory surge suggests some of the pre-tariff stockpiling impulse that drove copper's recent high is unwinding — though the longer-term supply deficit thesis from electrification and AI infrastructure demand remains intact, and project economics at $13,500-$14,000 copper are still strongly positive.

headline: GOLD'S TREASURY-DRIVEN RALLY FACES ITS RATE TEST — MINERS THAT AMPLIFIED EVERY MOVE NOW FACE JACKSON HOLE AND GDP DATA
snippet: Gold's five-consecutive-week rally has been structurally driven by the U.S. Treasury's expansion of long-bond buybacks, which compressed real yields and pushed the Dollar Index to a three-month low — conditions that are gold's most reliable near-term tailwind. Mining equities amplified each leg of the move: GDX gained 23.75% in August, and the GDXJ broke out of a four-month falling wedge as retail investors returned with $419 million in monthly ETF inflows. This week's macro data slate — Q2 GDP, Core PCE, ADP, and the Jackson Hole symposium where new Fed Chair Warsh will speak for the first time — represents the rate test that will determine whether the Treasury-driven dynamic holds or faces a fundamental challenge. For retail investors holding positions in TSX-V and ASX gold juniors, understanding the mechanism behind the rally is critical: if the move is real-yield driven rather than momentum-driven, it is more likely to persist through short-term data volatility than a speculative-led run.
